newsitem.title: USA: ABC Rail says files for $50 mln note offer.
newsitem.headline: ABC Rail says files for $50 mln note offer.

text.p: ABC Rail Products Corp said Friday it filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission a preliminary prospectus supplement to offer $50 million in senior subordinated notes due 2004.
The proposed sale to the public is expected to commence on or about January 28, 1997.
Don MacDonald, chief financial officer, said the note offering is part of a previously announced $100 million shelf offering of debt or equity.
The proposed notes will pay interest monthly at a rate to be determined, ABC said.

The notes will not be redeemable prior to January 15, 1999. The notes will be redeemable after that date and through January 14, 2000, at the option of the company at 102 percent of the principal amount, plus accrued and unpaid interest.
On or after January 15, 2000, the notes will be redeemable at 100 percent of the principal amount, plus accrued and unpaid interest.
The notes will be unsecured general obligations and will be subordinated to all senior debt, it added.
Proceeds will be used to repay certain debt.
ABC Rail makes and markets replacement products and original equipment for railroads and the rail transit industry.
